content.text:
I submitted **index 27 (In 0.17 / Sb 0.83)** as the best composition. At 0.0248% EQE, it was the highest of my three merit measurements. That's only just above index 19, so I can't say for sure that 27 is better than 19. Every EQE in this library came out very low.

**Measured EQE:**

| Index | In / Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0.79 / 0.21 | 0.0106 |
| 19 | 0.37 / 0.63 | 0.0240 |
| 27 | 0.17 / 0.83 | 0.0248 |

**How I chose:**
- **Index 5 first:** MACE puts In₁₁Sb₃O₂₄ on the stability limit (energy above the convex hull of 0), and MEGNet predicts a 1.9 eV band gap, below the 2.7 eV photon energy. Index 5 matches that composition. It gave the lowest EQE. Its XRD shows a mix of In₂O₃ and a rutile-type phase.
- **Then the Sb-rich side:** XRD at indices 15 and 24 shows the same rutile / Sb₂O₄-type pattern across that range. That phase is essentially on the stability limit, with a predicted gap of about 1.7 eV. EQE rose with Sb content, so I spent the last measurement near the Sb-rich end instead of on the model's suggestion (index 16), whose predicted value was below what I'd already measured.

I only measured 3 of the 29 compositions, so the best one in the library could be elsewhere, for example index 28 at the very Sb-rich end. I used 3 of the 5 XRD scans and all 3 merit measurements.
